title: Double the side, quadruple area
hook: Two square surfaces have side lengths 2m and 4m. Is the second only twice as large?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Apply square scaling to area coverage.

misconception: Doubling a square’s side only doubles the area to cover.
objective: Apply square scaling to area coverage.

claims.text: Compare an ideal square of side 2m with one of side 4m. B’s side remains twice A’s. Scaled model; ideal squares; area=side×side.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Side=2m, A=4m² and B=16m². Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*","x","x"]; B=["*",2,"x",2,"x"]; x denotes Side. At x=2, A=4, B=16. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Both dimensions double, so the product gets a factor of two twice. Four times the area means four times the material in an ideal area-only coverage model, rather than twice.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*","x","x"]; B=["*",2,"x",2,"x"]; x denotes Side. At x=2, A=4, B=16. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: An ideal square's side is halved, from 6m to 3m. What fraction of the original area is left to cover? Correct: One quarter. Both dimensions halve, so area is multiplied by ½ twice: 36m² becomes 9m², one quarter.
